title: Circumcision a seal of faith's righteousness — promise covers women and pre-day-eight males (Rom. 4; Lombard)
source_text: XIX. Sed quicquid hac de re dicant, vel sentiant adversarii, nos cum Apostolo dicimus circumcisionem fuisse, non remedium aliquod cujus externa applicatione tolleretur statim & aboleretur peccatum originale, sed, ut loquitur Apostolus, Sigillum justitiae fidei, Rom. 4. Itaque verum justitiae medium, & originalis peccati remedium in adultis omnibus, tam viris quam foeminis, fuit fides promissionibus divinis adhibita. Ista vero promissio quam fides accipiebat, & a qua gratia & salus pendebat, erat haec Abrahamo facta, Ero Deus tuus & seminis tui post te; sub quo semine non masculi solum, sed foeminae quoque comprehendebantur. Hujus promissionis virtute, non autem externi alicujus signi, Deus originale peccatum condonabat omnibus infantibus qui ante usum rationis in foedere moriebantur, sive circumcisionem illi accepissent, sive propter sexum muliebrem, aut aetatem immaturam, illam non accepissent. Quod vero cujusque familiae masculis circumcisionis signum imprimebatur, hoc promissionem toti familiae obsignabat, & in masculis foeminae Deo consecrabantur. Et certe quod absque externo sacramento in proprio corpore suscepto potuerint olim servari foeminae sub Veteri Testamento, & etiam masculi ante octavum diem, ex Lombardo poterat discere Bellarminus. Is enim lib. 4. dist. 1. litter. G. docet mulieres olim salutem & justitiam adeptas fuisse per fidem & operationem bonam, vel suam, si adultae erant, vel parentum, si parvulae. Et similiter parvulos ante circumcisionem in fide parentum servatos fuisse, idque Gregorii Papae testimonio confirmat.
pass_a_gloss: But whatever the adversaries say or think on this point, we with the Apostle say that circumcision was not some remedy by whose external application original sin was at once taken away and abolished, but, as the Apostle speaks, a Seal of the righteousness of faith, Rom. 4. Therefore the true means of righteousness, and the remedy of original sin in all adults, men as well as women, was faith applied to the divine promises. And that promise which faith received, and on which grace and salvation depended, was this made to Abraham: I will be your God and of your seed after you; under which seed not males only but women also were comprehended. By the virtue of this promise, not of any external sign, God remitted original sin to all infants who died in the covenant before the use of reason, whether they had received circumcision or, because of female sex or immature age, had not received it. And that the sign of circumcision was impressed on the males of each family sealed the promise to the whole family, and in the males the women were consecrated to God. And certainly that women of old could be saved under the Old Testament, and even males before the eighth day, without an external sacrament received in their own body, Bellarmine could have learned from Lombard. For he in book 4, distinction 1, letter G, teaches that women of old attained salvation and righteousness through faith and good operation — their own if adults, or their parents' if infants — and likewise that little ones before circumcision were saved in the faith of their parents, and he confirms it by the testimony of Gregory the Pope.
pass_b_english: With Paul we call circumcision a seal of the righteousness of faith (Rom. 4), not a rite that by outward application wiped original sin away.
Adults — men and women — were set right by faith in the divine promises.
Abraham's promise, I will be your God and of your seed, covered women as well as men.
By that promise God remitted original sin to covenant infants who died before reason, circumcised or not — including girls and boys before day eight.
Male circumcision sealed the promise for the whole household.
Even Lombard (and Gregory) taught Bellarmine that women and pre-circumcision infants were saved by faith — their own or their parents' — without a bodily sacrament.
